question: Correlation of -0.85 between two variables means:
before: -0.85 is strong negative: when one goes up, other reliably goes down. A describes r~0. C conflates correlation with causation. D incorrect -- anything above +/-0.7 is strong.
after:
Concept: Correlation measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two variables on a scale from -1 to +1. A correlation of -0.85 indicates both magnitude (closeness to -1) and direction (negative sign).

Why this is correct: A correlation of -0.85 is a strong negative correlation because its absolute value (0.85) exceeds the 0.7 threshold commonly used to define "strong" relationships, and the negative sign means the variables move in opposite directions — when one increases, the other reliably decreases.

Why the others are wrong: Option A claims no relationship, but a correlation of 0 or near-zero would show no relationship; -0.85 shows a definite and strong one. Option C confuses correlation with causation; correlation describes co-movement but does not establish that one variable causes the other to decline. Option D misidentifies the strength as weak, when any absolute value above 0.7 is conventionally considered strong.

Intuition: In equity research, a correlation of -0.85 between, say, interest rates and stock prices signals a reliable inverse pattern useful for hedging or sector rotation strategies, but the analyst must never assume the interest rate decline caused the stock price rise — only that they move together systematically.
